speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and how frequent the vomiting is? Have you noticed any blood in the stool, or any abdominal distension or tenderness upon examination?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus.

The onset of bilious vomiting within six hours of life in a newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, making volvulus the primary concern over other causes like pyloric stenosis which typically presents later with non-bilious vomiting.
